claim: For every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 4 with gcd(D)=1 and sigma(D)=sum_{d in D}1/(d-1)>1, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labels (d,j) with d in D and j>=k admit an explicitly recursive infinite sequence Q of distinct remaining labels with strictly increasing numerical values q_i, such that its actual complement R has finite subset sums with all consecutive gaps at most g=ceil(sum_{d in D}d^k/(d-1)+sum_{(d,j) in F}d^j), every base d in D occurs infinitely often in Q with bounded gaps between its selected exponents, and sum_i ||beta q_i||^2=infinity for every nonzero beta in R/Z; moreover for every integer L>=1 the finite subset sums of all remaining labels contain L consecutive integers with a terminating witness procedure, each label used at most once and coincident values from distinct labels retained separately.

quadruple.statement: For every nonempty finite set D of distinct integers at least 4 with gcd(D)=1 and sigma(D)=sum_{d in D}1/(d-1)>1, every integer k>=1 and every finite set F of labels (d,j) with d in D and j>=k admit an explicitly recursive infinite sequence Q of distinct remaining labels with strictly increasing numerical values q_i, such that its actual complement R has finite subset sums with all consecutive gaps at most g=ceil(sum_{d in D}d^k/(d-1)+sum_{(d,j) in F}d^j), every base d in D occurs infinitely often in Q with bounded gaps between its selected exponents, and sum_i ||beta q_i||^2=infinity for every nonzero beta in R/Z; moreover for every integer L>=1 the finite subset sums of all remaining labels contain L consecutive integers with a terminating witness procedure, each label used at most once and coincident values from distinct labels retained separately.
quadruple.stage: Classical additive number theory of labelled integer-power occurrences, with compact torus rotations and Fourier--Stieltjes averaging as proof tools.

shape.objects: Finite input D,k,F and an infinite pairwise-disjoint occurrence partition Q,R. Finite prefixes are proposed partial approximations extended by the least near-aligned cyclic power. Whether their fixed-gap and exponent-spacing constraints have common extensions is unknown. Integer powers, finite supports and the torus are standard objects; exact availability of the needed FS-mean formal library is unknown. Finite labelled-subset choices can also be made into Bernoulli random variables, as in the accepted CP25 spectral continuation; this is not a random-partition proof.
shape.quantifiers: For every finite strict-mass minimum-four gcd-one D, every positive cutoff k and finite labelled deletion F, construct one Q and its actual complement R with the stated fixed gap; every base has bounded selected exponent gaps, all nontrivial characters have divergent square mass, and every positive interval length has a finite legal witness returned by a terminating procedure. The leading quantifier is universal over finite inputs; its negation is one input for which no qualifying infinite partition/procedure exists. Individual characters range over R/Z, but the claim is not universal over arbitrary uncountable structures or all sets of reals.
shape.target_quantity: Existence of the explicitly recursive infinite partition with the specified exact gap bound g, bounded selected exponent gaps and all-length interval witnesses. This is not an extremal scalar, a density upper bound or a threshold-optimization problem; an unspecified replacement for the stated g would not settle it.
shape.ambient_structure: Labelled arithmetic and numerical order coexist with compact logarithmic phase recurrence and spectral averaging. Integer/rational finite tests and recursion supply a proposed one-label extension. The operation uses powers of each actual base; no simpler ambient carries every clause verbatim, and no pairwise-overlap or spread parameter for a random-partition proof has been recorded.
shape.symmetries: Base order only chooses a cyclic enumeration; finite occurrence deletions and coincidences must be respected. Translation can be used on numerical subset-sum sets in the transfer but does not translate the legal power labels. Arbitrary sparse extraction does not preserve selected exponent gaps; no intersection-closed structured-piece system with a bias statistic is asserted.
shape.configuration: Each Q label occurs once with strictly increasing value, every base occurs with bounded selected exponent gaps, and the actual complement R has gap at most g fixed in advance. The same Q must defeat every nontrivial character. Arbitrary deletion, restriction or truncation can destroy the infinite spectral and fixed-gap configuration. Near-aligned recursive extension is proposed to preserve it, but preservation is unproved.
shape.extremal_candidate: No extremal candidate or opposite-side optimal construction is named; the least eligible power is only a proposed local selection rule.
shape.finite_certificates: A finite interval and its finitely many labelled supports are checkable. A one-label seed is the smallest nonempty partial object at which a positive prefix margin can be sought analytically. These finite witnesses do not certify the infinite Q,R partition or the full universal claim, and no finite-domain process is admitted.
shape.monotonicity: For a fixed valid partition, an interval of larger length implies one of smaller length. The entire claim requires every positive length and all cutoffs/deletions, so no finite initial length settles it. No smallest isolated open finite instance of the full partition claim is recorded.
shape.uniformity_parameter: All strict-mass inputs with sigma(D)-1 arbitrarily small; all cutoff/deletion data; infinitely many selection stages and scales; every nonzero character and every interval length. The same g and Q must work throughout each fixed input. No common Fourier decay rate across characters is required.
shape.proof_shape: Planned iteration: first prove a phase-sensitive strict-prefix preservation lemma with explicit fixed tolerance and scale constants, then a positive one-label seed, bounded phase return/exponent gaps, the accepted spectral FS-mean transfer, legal intervals and procedure termination. No complete proof of this full claim is recorded. The iteration tracks coupled structural constraints, not independent scalar loss rows; no common formal class containing all stopped methods or finite solver residue is asserted. The final statement has explicit quantifiers, while its full new lemma chain remains unproved.
shape.neighbours: Known true: accepted CP25 removable-core partition and thickness, including the subfamily sigma(D)>=1+1/(min D-1) with H=D, which supplies every-base selected exponent gaps and the same g. Known true as a trusted literature interface: Griesmer's extreme-invariant/full-FS-mean sumset theorem. Open: the present strict-mass partition, the stronger existence of a thick proper supply disjoint from a bounded-gap reserve, equality at mass one, and general half-mass signed units. No proved property-reflecting categorical correspondence, verbatim simpler model, independent axiom variant, or computable refutation of the full partition claim is recorded.
shape.known_bounds: Acceptance-000012 proves the full required conclusion on sigma(D)>=1+1/(min D-1) via H=D; therefore a counterexample to this exact claim must lie below that threshold. Its equation(7) needs removable mass-one core for arbitrary latest selected base. Acceptance-000011's whole-base two-supply passage cannot reach total mass one and is not a barrier to this occurrence operation. No full unrestricted strict-mass construction, finite completeness reduction, first-moment random proof or uniform orbit-return numerical bound is recorded. No equivalence between the proposed preservation input and the full target is recorded.
shape.missing_input: An explicit phase-sensitive extension that preserves the fixed strict-prefix deficit at every scale while retaining bounded selected exponent gaps on the actual logarithmic orbit closure. This is a new unproved preservation lemma to establish, not a recognised external conjecture with an already proved exact threshold implication; it involves the original power geometry.
shape.base_theory: Ordinary classical mathematics with choice, within ZFC and compatible in principle with Lean's standard axioms. The objects are finite or countable supplies and compact metric groups, not an uncountable-cardinal independence problem. No additional guessing, forcing or independence axiom is proposed. Integer/rational witness checks can stay inside the base theory, but no finite check is admitted and the needed formal library has not been audited.

known: Accepted CP25, acceptance-000012, manifest73f908145b8601b3f44dc351f0ac5330620a8e315aefc7e4eaba6484c336cb1e, gives a fixed-gap cyclic spectral partition on the removable-core criterion and every-base selection when H=D; proof at ../erdos-124-cyclic-spectral-thinning/moves/001-cyclic-spectral-thinning.md.
Accepted CP24, acceptance-000011, supplies the sequential full FS-mean argument and the explicit two-supply completeness rung, with its stated method-specific threshold obstruction.

Burr, Erdos, Graham and Li, Complete sequences of sets of integer powers, DOI:10.4064/aa-77-2-133-138, states the original positive-cutoff finite-base conjecture and the Diophantine-approximation necessity observation; https://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/aa/aa77/aa7722.pdf.
Bergelson--Simmons arXiv:1507.02208v2, Claim2.13 footnote10, gives the compact group closure interface for a forward rotation orbit; targeted excerpt read.

Li--Oprocha--Ye--Zhang arXiv:1504.08191v1, Lemma2.1(2), states the classical all-neighborhood minimality/bounded positive returns interface; https://arxiv.org/html/1504.08191v1; journal DOI:10.1017/etds.2016.5.

Griesmer arXiv:2507.10512v1, Definition3.4, Lemma9.5(ii), Lemma10.3 and Corollary4.2(ii), provides the exact full FS-mean sumset interface; the published underlying Theorem3.17 is trusted, not independently reproved here.

The canonical original statement is Erdos124.erdos124.ne_zero in https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/main/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/124.lean; zero cutoff is distinct and not substituted.
